meta.title: Compresso: Instant Image Optimization in the Browser
meta.description: Tiny, zero dependency image optimizer. Compress, resize, and convert images on the client side with no server needed. Free and open source.
meta.ogTitle: Compresso: images optimized instantly, right in the browser
meta.ogDescription: A free image optimizer that runs entirely in your browser. Nothing is uploaded, and it works offline. Also available as a 3.6 KB library with HEIC input and Web Worker batching.

hero.title: Make images lighter, without uploading them anywhere.
hero.subtitle: Compresso compresses, resizes, and converts photos on your own device. Nothing is uploaded to a server, and it keeps working with no connection at all.

problem.label: Problem
problem.title: Uploads shouldn't fail.
problem.subtitle: Systems push compression, format conversion, and resizing onto the people least equipped to handle them, and the businesses that serve them pay the price.
problem.factsLead: The math doesn't work for ordinary users.
problem.stat1: of users abandon uploads due to file size errors
problem.stat3: common upload limit on government portals
problem.mockError: Your file is too large. Please upload an image under 2 MB.
problem.userQuote: Now what? How do I make it smaller?
problem.insight: The real gap isn't technical, it's cognitive. Users don't know how to preprocess images, and systems shouldn't ask them to.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.installDesc: Install via npm, yarn, or pnpm:
docs.cdnDesc: Or use directly from a CDN:
docs.compressDesc: Compresses a single image. Accepts a File, Blob, or image URL string.
docs.compressMultipleDesc: Compresses an array of files sequentially.
docs.createCompressorDesc: Creates a reusable compressor instance with preset options:
docs.targetSizeDesc: Set maxSizeMB to ensure the output never exceeds a given file size. Compresso uses binary search to find the highest quality that fits:
docs.batchWorkersDesc: New in 1.0.0: compresso.js/pool runs many compressions in parallel, off the main thread, via a resilient Web Worker pool — no UI jank on a 50-photo upload.
docs.batchWorkersNotes: createPool() never throws for lack of Worker support — it falls back to the exact same API on the main thread automatically. A worker that crashes or goes silent past a timeout is detected and replaced (visible via pool.stats().recoveries). compressMany() results are Promise.allSettled-shaped, so one failed file never sinks the rest of the batch.
docs.autoFormatDesc: When using format: 'auto', Compresso automatically detects the best format supported by the current browser.
docs.whyBrowserDesc: Client side optimization means the server receives an already optimized file. No server side processing, no GPU instances, no image processing libraries to maintain. The heavier the traffic, the more you save, because each user’s device does the work.

proof.label: Why it exists
proof.title: A size limit is a design failure that arrives as your fault.
proof.lede: A phone photo is routinely several megabytes. The form that rejects it allows five, and it will not tell you what to change. Compresso absorbs that problem back into the browser, where it takes under a second.
proof.oneDetail: Open your network tab and watch it stay silent while a hundred photos process.
proof.twoDetail: Results vary by content, so this is a single real result rather than an average we have not benchmarked.
proof.threeDetail: Zero required dependencies. Browser primitives only.

app.label: The app
app.title: Everything happens on your device.
app.lede: Free, installable, and built for the moment you have forty photos and a form that will not take any of them.
app.privateBody: There is no server to send your photos to. This is not a policy you have to trust, it is an architecture you can verify.
app.offlineBody: Install it once and it runs on a plane. The interface, the fonts, and the HEIC decoder are all stored on your device.
app.batchBody: Images are processed in parallel across your CPU cores, so the interface stays smooth while a large batch runs.
app.formatsBody: Reads HEIC, JPEG, PNG, WebP, and AVIF. Writes AVIF, WebP, JPEG, and PNG, choosing the best format your browser can produce.
app.langBody: English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, and Chinese, with sizes and percentages formatted the way each locale writes them.
app.shotAlt: Compresso in light mode, showing the same layout inverted to paper white and ink black.

library.label: For developers
library.title: The same engine, as a dependency.
library.lede: If you would rather your users never meet an upload error, the compression core ships as a library you can drop into any framework.
library.sizeBody: Small enough that adopting it does not need a meeting. Zero required dependencies, and nothing to audit.
library.workerTitle: Parallel batch compression, off the main thread
library.workerBody: compresso.js/pool runs a resilient Web Worker pool — crash and timeout recovery included — so a big batch compresses in parallel without blocking your interface.
library.guaranteeBody: Lossy output is capped at the smaller of your size limit and the original, because a compressor that can grow a file is broken.
